Business Foundations Mathematics: (21-120    Differential and Integral Calculus    or (21-111 & 21-112    Calculus I and Calculus II)) and (21-256    Multivariate Analysis    or 21-254    Linear Algebra and Vector Calculus for Engineers or 21-259    Calculus in Three Dimensions) and (70-257    Optimization for Business    or 21-257    Models and Methods for Optimization or 21-292    Operations Research I)
Business Foundations Economics: (73-102    Principles of Microeconomics     or 73-104    Principles of Microeconomics Accelerated) and 73-103    Principles of Macroeconomics and (73-230    Intermediate Microeconomics     or 73-240    Intermediate Macroeconomics)
Business Foundations Statistics: (70-207    Probability and Statistics for Business Applications    or 36-200    Reasoning with Data) and (70-208    Regression Analysis    or 36-202    Methods for Statistics & Data Science)
Business Core: 70-110    Business Computing and 70-122    Introduction to Accounting and 70-311    Organizational Behavior and 70-332    Business, Society and Ethics and 70-340    Business Communications and 70-345    Business Presentations and 70-371    Operations Management and 70-381    Marketing I and 70-391    Finance and 70-401    Management Game
Electives Requirement: Students must also complete a minimum of 18 units with a maximum of 21 units in Business courses (70-3xx). The electives cannot include the Business Leadership Endeavor courses (70-104 Business Leadership Endeavor I, 70-204 Business Leadership Endeavor II, 70-304 Business Leadership Endeavor III​) and Independent Study/Internship courses.
Credit Double Counting: Students pursuing the additional major may double-count two courses with any other major or minor requirements and are allowed unlimited double-counts for the business foundation courses. There are no double counting restrictions between the additional major and a student's home college general education requirements.
Notes: Students are eligible to apply for the Additional Major in Business Administration after completion of the Minor in Business Administration requirements plus 21-120 Differential and Integral Calculus and 70-207 Probability and Statistics for Business Applications (or equivalent course).
